title: Order book
description: A canvas price ladder: asks above the spread row, bids below, with depth bars, price grouping, flashes on changed levels, large order highlight and a cumulative hover summary. Hundreds of updates a second cost one draw per frame.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: book takes a snapshot ([price, size] levels in any order). The rows fill the height; the spread row shows the mid (or lastPrice) with the spread in basis points, the bar at the bottom the bid/ask imbalance. Hover a row: average price, sum and notional from the best level.

examples.title: Compact (mobile)
examples.description: A phone panel: two columns, 17 px rows, no imbalance bar, as many rows as the height allows (or set rows). Below 260 px wide the texts shrink and the third column is dropped.

examples.title: Dark terminal
examples.description: The ladder reads the CSS variables of its container: a terminal palette set on a wrapper (or the dark site theme). A monospace font aligns the digits; total="quote" shows the cumulative notional in USDT, depthBars="level" one bar per level.

examples.title: Price grouping
examples.description: grouping aggregates the levels by a price step: bids rounded down, asks up, so buckets never cross. The price decimals follow the step. depthBars draws cumulative or per-level bars.

examples.title: Large orders
examples.description: Levels reaching largeOrderThreshold are tinted, marked and bold. A click (or Enter) on a row fires onLevelClick with its cumulative values, e.g. to fill an order form.

examples.title: High-frequency stream
examples.description: A simulated matching engine sends 10 to 200 messages a second through the ref handle: applyDeltas for the book, setLastPrice for the trades. Changed levels flash (side color when they grow, gray when they shrink); each message costs a few array writes, the ladder draws once per frame and stops off screen.

examples.title: Asset classes
examples.description: One ladder for crypto, US equities, FX and futures: formatPrice and formatSize apply each market's conventions (dollars and cents, round lots, compact millions of euros, contracts), labels renames the columns and largeOrderThreshold follows the usual size of each market.

examples.title: Sides
examples.description: mode shows both sides, or only the bids or the asks: one side then fills the whole height. The arrow keys move through the rows, Enter picks one.

examples.title: Order ticket
examples.description: onLevelClick fills a ticket: a click on an ask prepares a buy at that price for the cumulative size (sum), a click on a bid a sell. The preview walks the book: what crosses fills at once with its average price, the rest queues behind the size already resting.

examples.title: Red up, green down
examples.description: colorConvention="red-up": red bids, green asks (mainland China, Japan, Korea). The flashes, depth bars, imbalance bar and last price arrow follow.

examples.title: Market terminal
examples.description: One simulated feed drives three widgets, the ladder, the depth chart and the trade tape, like one exchange WebSocket. Click a level: its price becomes a limit line on the depth chart. React only re-renders the header, four times a second.

examples.title: Wall watch (spoofing)
examples.description: The deltas passed to applyDeltas are also compared with the previous size of each level: a jump of 5 BTC or more is a new wall, highlighted by largeOrderThreshold. When it leaves, the trades at its price tell whether it was filled or pulled before the price got there.
